 SRFTI row: Students, alumni demand independent inquiry 
 Trending IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das SRFTI row: Students, alumni demand independent inquiry 
 Priyanka Dasgupta / TNN / Updated: Nov 01, 2026, 08:14 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Students and alumni at Kolkata Press Club on Saturday Kolkata: At the Save SRFTI joint news conference held by students and alumni at the Kolkata Press Club, the SRFTI Students’ Union began with a screening of a video made with edited footage of events that happened since the clash on Sept 27. Reiterating their position for a resolution through purposeful dialogue and accountability, the alumni have put forward three core demands: prompt withdrawal of all punitive measures imposed on students, immediate removal of police personnel from campus and swift resumption of talks based on an independent probe into the attacks on Sept 27 and Oct 4. The alumni association "has taken upon themselves to form a fact-finding committee constituted of eminent personalities of the civil society". This committee will engage itself with the deposition of all the stakeholders present during the disturbing incidents and submit a report based on such depositions. A communique would be sent to the institution for suggesting anyone whom they deem fit to be a part of the committee. A press release of the alumni that was read out by SRFTI alumnus and cinematographer Basab Mullik stated: "The current Vice-Chancellor has called those times extraordinary. We agree. It is extraordinary that students who are knifed get a show caused by the administration. It is extraordinary that thugs and goons can jump over the gates and transgress with impunity, but FIR is lodged against the students instead. It is indeed extraordinary when students seeking refuge inside the campus, because they are threatened outside, are denied accommodation, but a whole contingent of police arrives in the middle of the night to safeguard the current Vice-Chancellor, who now feels threatened by a symbolic mashal march. " Another alumnus - film-maker Anirban Datta - who was also present at the press conference told TOI that he is in "complete solidarity" with the current students. "We commend the endurance and fortitude that they have shown for more than a month. It will not be misplaced to acknowledge that they also fight for us when they resist an infringement on secular spaces of liberal thinking and humanitarian ethos," Datta said. The union additionally demands the resignation of VC Santosh Ajmera and the unconditional revocation of all show-cause notices with assurances against further action. Their charter further calls for an independent alumni-led inquiry into campus violence, “the circumstances surrounding the permission granted to the RSS-affiliated organisation to hold an event at the Main Theatre, and the role and accountability of the institute administration”. It also calls for bye-laws amendments “to ensure that external organisations permitted to use SRFTI premises are limited to those associated with cinema and filmmaking, with prior consultation and discussion involving all relevant stakeholders before any such permission is granted”. Raka Dutta, a fourth-batch alumna and head the the department of direction and screenplay writing at KR Narayanan Film Institute in Kerala as a professor, expressed solidarity with the students. Criticising the administration, she stated that “criminalising students and treating them like outsiders in their own institute where they are the primary stakeholders is completely unethical”. She added that “the administration has failed to serve its duty as a custodian/protector,” pointing out that students were assaulted in their own space while the administration framed it as a disciplinary matter. “But, no measures were taken against the so-called people who acted as goons, by pelting stones, glass,” she said. Cinematographer Manas Bhattacharyya from the fifth batch, who is currently based in Mumbai and receiving accolades for his work in Vinod Kapri's "Pyre", said, “Students being assaulted on campus by outsiders can’t be accepted. They are not getting any answer about why incidents happened. What is worse is the absence of security from the administration. Instead of providing a safe environment, they are subjected to surveillance and some have also been rusticated. Since we have not sufficient evidence to believe why they have been rusticated, it is difficult to accept the rational that this was a much-needed disciplinary action. Why students need to beg for security and welfare from the administration? This should come to them by default. The 24-hour deadline given for hostel vacation was inhuman. I am in agreement with the students about the VC’s resignation since there is enough evidence to suggest that he has become inhuman and is keen on only satisfying his ego.” SRFTI registrar Deepak Kumar said, “The video presented at the news conference offers a selective and edited account. The institute has taken sustained measures to ensure safety, address female students’ cyber-safety concerns and provide psychological support. Disciplinary action against students have been based on specific acts of misconduct, including threats, intimidation and assault — not participation in general protests. Any suggestion otherwise is factually incorrect. ” SRFTI VC Santosh Ajmera said, “Our faculty members are actively engaging with students to understand their genuine concerns and grievances. We remain hopeful that continued dialogue and mutual understanding will help resolve the situation soon and restore normal academic life.”
